explanation.text:
(Pro. 20:1-30)

mocker--scorner. Such men are made by wine.

strong drink--made by spicing wine (compare Isa 5:11, Isa 5:22); and it may include wine.

raging--or boisterous as a drunkard.

deceived--literally, "erring," or reeling.

bsb.text: Wine is a mocker, strong drink is a brawler, and whoever is led astray by them is not wise.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 19:12). Men who resist authority injure themselves (Rom 13:2).

bsb.text: The terror of a king is like the roar of a lion; whoever provokes him forfeits his own life.

explanation.text:
to cease from strife--or, better, "to dwell from or without strife," denoting the habit of life.

fool . . . meddling-- (Pro 17:14).

bsb.text: It is honorable for a man to resolve a dispute, but any fool will quarrel.

explanation.text: shall . . . beg--literally, "ask" (in this sense, Psa 109:10).

bsb.text: The slacker does not plow in season; at harvest time he looks, but nothing is there.

explanation.text: Counsel . . . water--that is, deeply hidden (Pro 18:4; Psa 13:2). The wise can discern well.

bsb.text: The intentions of a man’s heart are deep waters, but a man of understanding draws them out.

explanation.text:
Boasters are unreliable.

goodness--or, "kind disposition."

bsb.text: Many a man proclaims his loving devotion, but who can find a trustworthy man?

explanation.text: The conduct of good men proclaims their sound principles. God's covenant and their good example secure blessing to their children (Pro 4:26; Psa 112:1-2).

bsb.text: The righteous man walks with integrity; blessed are his children after him.

explanation.text: As in Pro 14:35; Pro 16:10, Pro 16:15, this is the character of a good king, not of all kings.

bsb.text: A king who sits on a throne to judge sifts out all evil with his eyes.

explanation.text: The interrogation in the affirmative strengthens the implied negation (compare Job 15:14; Ecc 7:20).

bsb.text: Who can say, “I have kept my heart pure; I am cleansed from my sin”?

explanation.text: Various measures, implying that some are wrong (compare Pro 11:1; Pro 16:11).

bsb.text: Differing weights and unequal measures—both are detestable to the LORD.

explanation.text: The conduct of children even is the best test of principle (compare Mat 7:16).

bsb.text: Even a young man is known by his actions—whether his conduct is pure and upright.

explanation.text: Hence, of course, God will know all you do (Psa 94:9).

bsb.text: Ears that hear and eyes that see—the LORD has made them both.

explanation.text:
Activity and diligence contrasted with sloth (Pro 6:9; Pro 10:11).

lest . . . poverty--literally, "be deprived of inheritance."

bsb.text: Do not love sleep, or you will grow poor; open your eyes, and you will have plenty of food.

explanation.text: when . . . his way--implying that he goes about boasting of his bargains.

bsb.text: “Worthless, worthless!” says the buyer, but on the way out, he gloats.

explanation.text: The contrast denotes the greater value of knowledge (compare Pro 3:14-16).

bsb.text: There is an abundance of gold and rubies, but lips of knowledge are a rare treasure.

explanation.text:
Take his garment--implies severe exaction, justified by the surety's rashness.

a strange woman--by some readings "strangers," but the former here, and in Pro 27:13, is allowable, and strengthens the sense. The debauchee is less reliable than the merely careless.

bsb.text: Take the garment of the one who posts security for a stranger; get collateral if it is for a foreigner.

explanation.text:
Bread . . . sweet--either as unlawfully (Pro 9:17) or easily obtained.

mouth . . . gravel--well expresses the pain and grief given at last.

bsb.text: Food gained by fraud is sweet to a man, but later his mouth is full of gravel.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 15:22). Be careful and considerate in important plans.

bsb.text: Set plans by consultation, and wage war under sound guidance.

explanation.text:
Those who love to tell news will hardly keep secrets.

flattereth . . . lips--(compare Margin; Pro 1:10).

meddle . . . him--literally, "join," or "associate with."

bsb.text: He who reveals secrets is a constant gossip; avoid the one who babbles with his lips.

explanation.text: his lamp--(Compare Pro 13:9; Pro 24:20).

bsb.text: Whoever curses his father or mother, his lamp will be extinguished in deepest darkness.

explanation.text: gotten hastily--contrary to God's providence (Pro 28:20), implying its unjust or easy attainment; hence the man is punished, or spends freely what he got easily (compare Pro 20:17).

bsb.text: An inheritance gained quickly will not be blessed in the end.

explanation.text: (Compare Psa 27:14; Rom 12:17-19).

bsb.text: Do not say, “I will avenge this evil!” Wait on the LORD, and He will save you.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 20:10; Pro 11:1).

bsb.text: Unequal weights are detestable to the LORD, and dishonest scales are no good.

explanation.text:
Man's goings--literally, "Stately steppings of a strong man."

a man--any common man.

understand--or, "perceive."

bsb.text: A man’s steps are from the LORD, so how can anyone understand his own way?

explanation.text: devoureth . . . holy--or, better, "who rashly speaks promises," or "devotes what is holy," consecrating any thing. This suits better the last clause, which expresses a similar view of the results of rashly vowing.

bsb.text: It is a trap for a man to dedicate something rashly, only later to reconsider his vows.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 20:8).

bringeth . . . over them--The wheel was used for threshing grain. The figure denotes severity (compare Amo 1:3).

bsb.text: A wise king separates out the wicked and drives the threshing wheel over them.

explanation.text: The spirit . . . Lord--Men's minds are God's gifts, and thus able to search one another (compare Pro 20:5; Pro 18:8, Pro 18:17; Co1 2:11).

bsb.text: The spirit of a man is the lamp of the LORD, searching out his inmost being.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 3:3; Pro 16:6, Pro 16:12).

bsb.text: Loving devotion and faithfulness preserve a king; by these he maintains his throne.

explanation.text: The glory of young men . . . the beauty of old men--Each age has its peculiar excellence (Pro 16:31).

bsb.text: The glory of young men is their strength, and gray hair is the splendor of the old.

explanation.text:
blueness--literally, "joining," the process of uniting the edges of a wound throws off purulent matter.

stripes . . . belly--So punishment provides healing of soul (Pro 18:8), by deterring from evil courses.

Next: Proverbs Chapter 21

bsb.text: Lashes and wounds scour evil, and beatings cleanse the inmost parts.
